display.purpose: Hero headlines only. One per page. Bricolage Grotesque with optical sizing.

title.purpose: Event card titles, card-level headings. Two-line clamp.

body.purpose: Paragraph text. Cap line length at 65-75ch. Inter 16px / 1.55.

meta.purpose: Quiet labels above or beside primary content (eyebrows, taglines, summary lines, captions). Inter 13px sentence case, muted color.

numeric.purpose: Dates, times, location coordinates, identifiers, calendar grid numbers. IBM Plex Mono 11-12px, light tracking ≤0.06em, sentence case.

shadows.name: card
shadows.purpose: Ambient lift for resting cards and elevated surfaces. Subtle enough to be felt, not seen.

shadows.name: cardHover
shadows.purpose: Hover state on lifted cards. Pair with the 1px transform-Y lift.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: The system's only easing. Decelerates without bounce. Used for state, hover, entrance, scroll-reveal.

motion.name: duration-state
motion.purpose: Default duration for state transitions (color, opacity, border).

motion.name: duration-transform
motion.purpose: Hover transforms (translateY, scale) and inline icon shifts.

motion.name: duration-entrance
motion.purpose: Fade-up entrance animations on first paint.

narrative.overview: Highlander Hub is the screen-side stand-in for the physical UCR campus: many voices, edited gathering, a place rather than a tool. The interface is a place a student passes through, glances at, and leaves having seen something they wouldn't have seen otherwise. It is not a search engine, not a feed, not a marketplace. It is a quad with a bulletin in it. The system reads as edited and paper-confident: display type does the work, chrome stays hairline-thin, and the page is built to be skimmed in five seconds before it asks for any commitment. Color is tightly rationed and meaningful (the category palette is the only place hue lives); everything else sits in tinted neutrals.
keyCharacteristics: Hairline-bordered surfaces; depth via 1px lifts, not shadow blooms (current state; moving toward subtle ambient shadow).
Bricolage Grotesque display + Inter body + IBM Plex Mono labels. No fourth font.
Restrained color strategy: category accents at ≤10% of any surface.
Mobile-first: every layout is designed for a phone first.
Motion is decelerating-only (ease-out-expo), no bounce, no elastic, reduced-motion honored at the root.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Category color appears as a tinted background (/10 or /15 opacity), never as a saturated fill behind body content. Total accent coverage on any screen stays at or below 10% of the surface. Saturated category color appears in exactly one place: the 4px category rail on the left edge of EventCard.

rules.name: The Tinted-Neutral Rule
rules.body: No new pure-hex grayscale values. Every neutral tints toward the cool ink hue. If you need a step between surface and line, derive it from the existing ramp.

rules.name: The Meaning-Carrying Rule
rules.body: Hue is for category. If a UI element uses color but is not signaling a category, it is wrong. Promotional accents, decorative gradients, mood-color washes: prohibited.

rules.name: The One-Display Rule
rules.body: Bricolage Grotesque is the only display face. Inter is the only body face. IBM Plex Mono is the only mono. No fourth font is added without retiring one of the three.

rules.name: The Tracking Rule
rules.body: Display type tracks tight (-0.02em to -0.035em). Body and labels use normal tracking; numeric mono uses ≤0.06em. Tracked-out uppercase (tracking-[0.12em] and friends, in any font) is prohibited as a decorative label pattern — it is the SaaS / dev-tool reflex the AI Slop Test rejects.

rules.name: The Quiet-Label Rule
rules.body: Eyebrows, taglines, summary lines, and captions render in Inter, sentence case, small (12-13px), normal tracking, muted color. No uppercase. No tracked-out caps. No mono-as-decoration. IBM Plex Mono is reserved for genuinely numeric content (dates, times, coordinates, identifiers), never for label decoration. Replaces the retired Eyebrow-Mono Rule.

rules.name: The Hairline-Plus-Lift Rule
rules.body: Edges live in 1px borders tinted from ink. Depth is a 1px translate on hover, optionally with a tonal shadow. No glow, no double-shadow, no inner shadow.

rules.name: The Quiet-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are tonal (ink-tinted) and low-opacity (≤0.08). No black shadows. No colored shadows. Two flavors: card shadow (small blur, ≤12px primary / ≤28px diffusion) for resting / hover lift on cards; sticky-overlay halo (large blur up to ~40px at ≤0.08 opacity) for separating a sticky glass surface from scrolling content. Outside those flavors, if the blur is visible enough to describe from across the room it is too strong.

rules.name: The Three-Glass Rule
rules.body: Glass (backdrop-blur, frosted surfaces) is sanctioned in exactly three places: the Masthead glass variant, the image-overlay Category Pill on Event Cards, and the /events sticky filter bar. Glass is never a default surface; new glass usages require updating this rule.

dos: Do keep the hue-as-meaning discipline: color signals category, full stop.
Do use Bricolage Grotesque for any display or headline role, Inter for body, IBM Plex Mono for labels, dates, and times.
Do keep eyebrows, taglines, and summary lines quiet: Inter, small (12-13px), sentence case, normal tracking, muted color. The 'edited bulletin caption' look, not the 'SaaS landing eyebrow' look.
Do reserve IBM Plex Mono for content that is genuinely numeric (dates, times, coordinates, identifiers), never as decorative label-style.
Do prefer hairline-bordered surfaces (border-ink/10 to border-ink/15) over background-tinted ones for default cards and rows.
Do ease motion out only (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)). Durations: 180-300ms for state, 700-800ms for entrance.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion on anything you add.
Do treat the FlyerMosaic image-card and the text-with-category-rail variant as the two canonical ways to render an event.
Do use the .interactive-focus global class on every interactive element.
Do size for a phone first. Touch targets ≥44×44px.
donts: Don't ship the generic SaaS landing look. No hero-metric templates, no identical icon-heading-text card grids, no gradient text.
Don't ship university .edu CMS energy. No institutional navy headers, no brochure-density link soup.
Don't ship the Eventbrite / Meetup transactional look. No ad-cluttered list rows, no RSVP-button stripes.
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent on any component except the sanctioned Category Rail on text-variant Event Cards.
Don't use background-clip: text with a gradient. Gradient text is decorative-only and never carries meaning here.
Don't introduce new pure-#000 or pure-#fff values in any new code.
Don't apply glassmorphism outside the three sanctioned uses: the Masthead glass variant, the image-overlay Category Pill, and the /events sticky filter bar. (The Three-Glass Rule.)
Don't stack cards inside cards. Nested cards are always wrong.
Don't reach for a modal as a first thought.
Don't bounce or elastic motion. Ease-out only.
Don't animate CSS layout properties. Transform and opacity only.
Don't write em dashes in UI copy.
Don't decorate labels, eyebrows, taglines, or section headers with uppercase + tracking in any font. That pattern is the SaaS / dev-tool reflex the AI Slop Test rejects.
Don't add a fourth font, a fourth radius scale, or a sixth typography step without retiring an existing one.
